clue.text: Mysterious result of using rotation system on farm?

definitions.text: Mysterious result of using rotation system on farm?

parts.words: Mysterious result of using rotation system on farm?
parts.note: a farming term, crop rotation, is read literally as a field of grain spun into a ring, the unexplained flattened patterns found in fields

explanation.surface: A puzzled observer wonders what strange outcome a farm's rotation scheme has produced.
explanation.definitionFit: The flattened rings that appear overnight in fields of wheat are famously unexplained, so they are a mysterious agricultural result.

clue.text: Whip-round for old statesman

parts.note: a cat (cat-o'-nine-tails) is a whip
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A collection is taken among colleagues for a retired politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip-round' looks like one word for a collection; split it into a whip and a round.
explanation.definitionFit: Cato the Elder was a Roman statesman of the second century BC.

clue.text: Moves on board,'initially, given opportunity

definitions.meaning: the first series of moves in a game of chess is called by this name
a chance or ... for someone to get in

explanation.surface: A player's early moves in a board game give them a chance.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess's first moves have this name, and a chance or vacancy is also called one.

clue.text: Encouragement for a lot of pupils to go into production

parts.note: 'come on!' is a shout of encouragement
a stream is a group of pupils of similar ability in a school year

explanation.surface: A school urges a group of pupils to start work in manufacturing.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant or project that starts operating is said idiomatically to begin producing output at last.

clue.text: Jam session?

parts.note: a musicians' improvising get-together is reread as a period of traffic jams, the busy commuting time

explanation.surface: Musicians gather for an informal improvised performance.
explanation.definitionFit: The commuting peak is when roads are jammed, so it is a period of traffic congestion.

clue.text: Apt subject

definitions.meaning: apt means likely or inclined to do something
subject to something means exposed or open to it

explanation.definitionFit: One is liable to do something when inclined, and liable to a tax or fine when exposed to it.

clue.text: Feature of Roman calendar that is cut

indicators.note: cut means the end of the Latin phrase is docked, losing its final letter

parts.note: id est is Latin for 'that is', abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: Someone describes an element of the Roman calendar that was dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the final T of ID EST, leaving IDES; the Latin phrase suits the Roman theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romans marked mid-month with this day, the 15th of March, May, July and October, the 13th otherwise.

clue.text: Precisely criticise, showing no emotion.

parts.note: dead means exactly, as in 'dead on time'
to pan a show is to criticise it harshly

explanation.surface: A critic delivers an exact put-down with a straight face.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadpan delivery is expressionless, a poker face giving nothing away.

clue.text: Second chap destroyed without money

parts.note: Tony is any man's name, a chap
broke means broken, smashed

explanation.surface: A second man is ruined and left penniless.
explanation.walkthrough: STONY-BROKE is British slang for completely penniless.
explanation.definitionFit: Being completely penniless is the meaning of this British slang phrase.

clue.text: Device needed, as being dreadfully hot matters

indicators.note: dreadfully suggests things in a terrible mess, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gadget is required because heat is causing terrible problems.
explanation.definitionFit: A temperature-regulating device switches heating on and off.

clue.text: Mexican food buried in catacomb

indicators.note: buried in says the letters lie inside the word catacomb, as if entombed there

explanation.surface: A Mexican snack is found entombed in an underground cemetery.
explanation.definitionFit: A folded tortilla with filling is a staple of Mexican cooking.

clue.text: Stop working and get off? Blimey!

parts.note: to strike is to stop work in a dispute
to alight is to get off a bus or train

explanation.surface: Someone stops work and gets off the train, exclaiming in surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: STRIKE A LIGHT is a dated British exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a British exclamation of astonishment, like 'Good heavens!'.

clue.text: Ring established by spies for so long

indicators.note: established by means the ring is set beside the spies, coming after them

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency, a body of spies
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A spy network is set up and runs for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so long' looks like a measure of time but is a farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian 'ciao' is an informal goodbye, like the casual farewell 'so long'.

clue.text: In serious trouble, he will excel? Yes

parts.note: he'll is the contraction of he will
to top is to beat or excel
ay (aye) means yes

explanation.surface: Someone in a fix wonders whether he will shine, and answers yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link: someone in serious trouble faces the phrase's consequence.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'there'll be ... ' means severe consequences or big trouble ahead.

clue.text: A lot of 'trouble taken by fisherman?

definitions.meaning: a messy situation full of complications once opened up
an angler carries a tin of bait, worms, to the riverbank

explanation.surface: An angler brings along plenty of bother.
explanation.definitionFit: Opening a source of complications is idiomatic for stirring up trouble, and literally a tin of bait.

clue.text: Emperor chubby as a lad

definitions.meaning: the first Roman emperor took this title
the greedy fat boy Gloop in Roald Dahl's Charlie and the Chocolate Factory has this first name

explanation.surface: A ruler is described as having been a plump boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Octavian took this name as first Roman emperor, and Dahl's greedy plump boy Gloop bears it too.

clue.text: Wife's shot is a successful one

parts.note: in archery or shooting, an inner is a shot hitting the ring next to the bull

explanation.surface: A woman's shot in competition is the one that wins.
explanation.definitionFit: A victor is someone who has succeeded, a successful one.

clue.text: A bad case' of wind catching one

indicators.note: catching means the wind captures the numeral inside itself

parts.note: the mistral is a cold northerly wind in southern France
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone suffers a nasty bout of flatulence, caught by one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' sounds medical; it is a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial declared invalid through error is a court case gone bad.

clue.text: City one passes through on way from Lincoln to Exeter

definitions.text: City one passes through on way from Lincoln to Exeter

parts.words: City one passes through on way from Lincoln to Exeter
parts.note: Lincoln and Exeter look like distant English cities but are also neighbouring colleges in one university town

explanation.surface: A traveller crosses England from the Midlands to Devon via a city.
explanation.walkthrough: A road trip from Lincoln to Exeter would pass many cities; the colleges of these names sit side by side in one university city.
explanation.definitionFit: Lincoln College and Exeter College are both in this university city, so walking between them keeps you in it.

clue.text: Drop support for scapegoat

parts.note: a fall is a drop
a guy is a rope supporting a tent or mast

explanation.surface: Someone abandons backing for a person to be blamed.
explanation.definitionFit: A patsy who takes the blame for others is a scapegoat.

clue.text: Associate party with enjoyment

parts.note: a side is a party in a dispute
a kick is a thrill or bit of enjoyment

explanation.surface: Someone links a party with having fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidekick is a close companion or partner, an associate.

clue.text: Frozen fish left inside under rocks

indicators.note: under means, in this down clue, the fish comes below the ice

parts.note: on the rocks means with ice, so rocks are ice

indicators.note: inside means the letter for left goes within the fish

parts.note: cod is a fish

explanation.surface: A fish left on ice becomes frozen.
explanation.definitionFit: Something chilled solid is extremely cold, frozen.

clue.text: Unnecessary fuss? It's fair game

definitions.meaning: a lot of commotion or ballyhoo over nothing
a fairground game of throwing rings over prizes

explanation.surface: Someone complains about pointless fuss but says it is a legitimate target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair game' suggests a legitimate target; here it is a game at a funfair.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both ballyhoo and the ring-tossing fairground stall game.

clue.text: In protest, depart without Jack for stroll

indicators.note: without means outside, so the departure phrase goes around the sailor

parts.note: to walk out is to leave in protest
a jack (jack tar) is a sailor, AB being an able seaman

explanation.surface: Someone storms off in protest, leaving Jack behind, for a walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here is the old sense 'outside', not 'lacking'.
explanation.definitionFit: A walkabout is a leisurely walk among people, as a royal does meeting a crowd.

clue.text: A number of Germans produced pork pies

definitions.meaning: a German art song, a number sung by Germans
pork pies is rhyming slang for lies, so this means told lies

explanation.walkthrough: PORK PIES is Cockney rhyming slang for lies.
explanation.definitionFit: A German art song has this name, and someone who told untruths did this.

clue.text: Perform song accompanied by piano

indicators.note: accompanied by means the song is set alongside, here after, the soft marking

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
a lay is a song or ballad

explanation.surface: A singer performs a song with piano accompaniment.
explanation.definitionFit: To play a piece is to perform it.

clue.text: Jazz tune, a basis for improvisation

parts.note: a rag is a ragtime piece, an early jazz tune

explanation.surface: A jazz number provides a framework for improvising.
explanation.definitionFit: In Indian classical music a melodic framework is the basis on which performers improvise.

clue.text: Bound to go round for Oriental snack

parts.note: to bound is to spring or leap
to roll is to go round, revolve

explanation.surface: Someone is bound to circle back for some Chinese food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' looks like 'certain to'; it is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastry roll with vegetable filling, fried, is a Chinese snack.

clue.text: Sort of sauce, say, spread over duck

indicators.note: over means the scrambled letters cover the duck, lying around it
spread means the letters of say are scattered out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a duck is zero in cricket, the letter O

explanation.surface: A kind of sauce is said to be poured over duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' rearranges SAY to SYA, which goes 'over' (around) O.
explanation.definitionFit: A bean-based condiment from East Asia is this sort of sauce.

clue.text: Ring Italian before 6, say, and decide to stop

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it
6 refers to the 6-across answer, a date in the Roman calendar, which is an example of a day

explanation.surface: Someone phones an Italian before six o'clock and then knocks off.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' looks like a time; it is a cross-reference to 6 across, the 15th of March etc., one day.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to stop working on something for now, to finish.
